answer: Make every identity pay in compute before it can act: a newcomer must solve a fresh proof-of-work puzzle bound to its own public key, about ten minutes of CPU time, and the puzzle expires within the hour so it cannot be stockpiled. One thin thread ties each solution to exactly one key, stamped in umber ink on the identity's record. A plume of a thousand fresh identities from one subnet faces a difficulty that doubles with each sibling, so the thousandth clone costs a thousand times the first. An honest agent pays ten minutes once; a farm pays in power and hardware it cannot fake.
